feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the experience is clearly progressive, relevant, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some structural overlap that reduces punch.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression within NACo into director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, video, and multi-channel communications.  
- Good credibility and impact signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms strengthen authority.  
- Writing is polished and generally error-free, with a modern, strategic tone aligned to public-sector digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics: include measurable improvements such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, search performance, campaign results, or cost savings.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs. “web, email, social and video”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)” instead. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats several competency areas listed elsewhere. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems, governance models and content operations. Led enterprise website transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics, editorial and multimedia systems that improve delivery, oversight and audience experience.”
- Replace “Leads” with “Led” or “Has led” for tense consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Add 1–2 proof points from recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Tighten the final list so it emphasizes differentiators rather than broad capability coverage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Enterprise web modernization” closely repeats the subtitle and multiple work-experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas with more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for faster scanning.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “website” with “web” and “communications operations” with “communications leadership” for a more senior tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences,” “analytics and reporting infrastructure,” and “multimedia production and livestream operations” repeat language already covered in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and Topline Skills; keep only if this audience focus is a key differentiator.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several points already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp line with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with more specific ones where possible: “Launched,” “Created,” “Produced,” “Designed.”
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” and “modular Drupal 10 microsite with interactive storytelling and downloadable resources.”
- Consider this style: “AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with NACo roles in Work Experience; keep this section framed as selected project examples, not a restatement.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” feels most distinct—good candidate to keep if space is tight.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level impact, transformation work, and only the newest/highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet on improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Replace generic phrasing (“deliver CMS development,” “advise on best practices”) with stronger verbs and outcomes: “Built,” “Launched,” “Redesigned,” “Standardized,” “Improved.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages, users, toolkits, teams supported, or efficiency gains.
- Emphasize consultant value-add: strategic advisory, implementation leadership, and AI search initiative; de-emphasize routine front-end troubleshooting unless it produced a notable result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal microsites, AI search, and campaign storytelling duplicate the Recent Projects section—keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also repeat the 2022–2024 NACo role; frame this as post-tenure advisory/modernization work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Prioritize the strongest achievements first and make them more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Condense channel oversight into one bullet and add measurable outcomes if available (open rates, follower growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings).
- Tighten wording on systems work: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio and expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery to improve reporting, planning and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older roles and Recent Projects; focus here on building the studio/capability, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, repeatability, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.” / “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Reframe vague bullets with stronger verbs: replace “Helped improve” with “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.”
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, turnaround-time improvements, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; position this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- “Editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this entry focused on execution and operationalization, not governance leadership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership/value angle and avoid repeating broad phrases already proven in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic labels with tighter, outcome-oriented skill phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging for mission-driven organizations
- Audience-centered content planning informed by analytics and user needs
- Consider dropping “public-sector and advocacy messaging” if space is tight; it is already well supported across recent experience.
- If formatting allows, keep to 4 bullets instead of 5 for more punch and less repetition.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than the analytics/governance strengths shown elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first; lead with strategic/enterprise strengths, then key platforms.
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)” unless jQuery is specifically required.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- If possible, align with outcomes from recent roles, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page sites” or “platforms supporting 3.5M annual page views,” though metrics fit better in experience bullets than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider using “search and discovery experiences” here to reduce repetition.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from pure tools to capability + decision impact, e.g.:
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity
- Analytics infrastructure and dashboard development
- KPI framework design and executive reporting
- SEO, content performance and conversion analysis
- Consider renaming to “Analytics Infrastructure, Reporting & Optimization” to better match seniority.
- Keep the most relevant tools first; group “Microsoft Clarity” with behavior insights rather than as a standalone item.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point tied to recent work (e.g. supported reporting for a 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates almost exactly with “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with the “Multimedia & live event production” competency plus multiple NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific, senior, and operations-focused rather than a basic task list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to capability + delivery scope:
- Video production, editing, and livestream direction
- Broadcast-quality studio and PTZ camera operations
- Hybrid, virtual, and live event production
- Run-of-show planning and technical event execution
- If accurate, add scale or complexity to signal impact, e.g. “multi-camera,” “broadcast-quality,” “executive-facing,” or “high-volume recurring programming.”
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid single-word fragments like “Livestreaming” when “livestream direction” is stronger.
- Optional tighter heading/content approach: “Multimedia & Event Production” with 4 bullets max.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production.”
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are already implied by the NACo studio-building achievement; don’t overemphasize both here unless they’re differentiators.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This item should either add specificity on level of use/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same CMS names twice.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, microsites, migration support) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first** and add a brief qualifier since it is clearly the most recent and highest-impact platform in your experience.
- If space is tight, cut **GitHub Pages** unless you can show meaningful professional use; it reads lighter than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**, which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Consider keeping platform names in only one section, and using this item instead for tools not named elsewhere or for proficiency/context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use it to signal level and modern relevance, not repeat basics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw tools to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery” rather than separate items.
- Prioritize current/recently used tools and stronger differentiators: keep API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions; consider dropping “HTML5/CSS3” styling if space is tight.
- Add scope or proficiency where accurate, e.g. “API integrations for CMS/content workflows,” “GitHub Actions for deployment automation,” “Cloudflare Workers for lightweight edge scripting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations for CMS/content workflows • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting) • GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- If Topline Skills stays, this section should be more implementation-specific or include only tools not named elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger workflow/systems claims elsewhere. Make it more selective and role-relevant, emphasizing automation/build systems over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems”
- Tighten to higher-signal tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- If accurate, add light qualifiers to show depth: “Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana (project operations)”
- Consider a stronger version if space allows: “Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery through Jira and Asana”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Slack, Teams, and Basecamp/Trello are low-value here; they read as everyday collaboration tools rather than differentiating technical skills.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills, so this item should stay concise and tool-focused rather than repeat capability language.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling platform depth and audience engagement relevance without repeating work-experience bullets.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Newsletter publishing workflows • Audience segmentation
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability instead of generic tools: Marketing automation • Journey orchestration • List management • A/B testing
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding audience size or newsletter frequency here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already captured in the summary and core competencies

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item is too generic and largely repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills section. It should either be tightened to emphasize technical execution or reduced to avoid overloading the CV with duplicate analytics keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward implementation-focused skills, not broad concepts: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation support • KPI dashboard development”
- Replace vague nouns like “Dashboarding” with stronger, resume-ready phrasing such as “KPI dashboard development” or “reporting automation.”
- Consider dropping “A/B testing” unless you can support it elsewhere with a concrete example or outcome in recent roles.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently used tools first: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity …”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [3]; keep one more strategic and this one strictly tool-based.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader digital strategy language; “SEO analysis” is more specific and less repetitive.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results where possible: website refresh scope, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the close to show supervision without overstating leadership: “Mentored a digital media associate on day-to-day production and publishing.”
- Possible version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo roles; specify what changed or cut it here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination scope and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch its own clause and tighten wording: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scale or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or types of materials delivered.
- Consider a more concise final version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for program and policy teams, supporting digital and multimedia content development. Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item higher-level and podcast-focused.
- Avoid claiming broad digital leadership here, since stronger evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
